seo.title: FAQ
seo.description: Answers on who the platform is for, what is included at launch, onboarding, pricing, and security assurances.

header.heading: Questions, answered plainly.
header.body: Straight answers on who the platform is for, what ships at launch, how onboarding runs, what it costs and how we handle your data. Nothing here sits behind a form.

items.title: Who is the Privacy Culture Platform designed for?
items.body: It is designed for mid-market privacy teams that need stronger oversight than spreadsheets provide, without taking on an enterprise-scale privacy platform implementation. Our focus is UK organisations with roughly 1,000 to 5,000 employees.

items.title: What is included at launch?
items.body: At launch, the platform includes Tasks, ROPA, Incidents, Vendors, Operational Assessments, and Risks. All modules are fully connected and included together rather than sold as separate feature-gated tiers.

items.title: Can you import our existing ROPA?
items.body: Yes. We import existing ROPA data from Excel as part of our assisted onboarding process to ensure your Visual ROPA View is live quickly.

items.title: How quickly can we get live?
items.body: Our launch commitment is to get your Visual ROPA View live within 30 days, subject to standard data availability, agreed scope, and customer participation.

items.title: Do you offer a free trial?
items.body: We do not offer an anonymous, self-serve trial at this time. Following a brief demo, controlled product access can be arranged once we understand your operational context and data structures.

items.title: How much does it cost?
items.body: Pricing starts at £500 per month for organisations with up to 750 employees, then £800 for 751–1,500, £1,250 for 1,501–3,000 and £1,667 for 3,001–5,000, each billed annually. Above 5,000 employees, or for complex groups, pricing is on application. Every plan is a 12-month agreement and includes all launch modules.

items.title: What security assurances are available?
items.body: Privacy Culture holds Cyber Essentials certification, and the Platform undergoes independent penetration testing. Detailed security collateral, including our standard DPA, is accessible directly on our dedicated Trust & Security page.

header.heading: Bring the awkward questions.
header.body: Book a demo and we will walk the platform through your own processing activities rather than a canned dataset.

data.micro: Our security collateral is published without a sales gate.

header.body: Scrambling before an audit or insurer assessment creates friction and reveals gaps. Maintain a continuous, time-stamped audit log of data inventory reviews and vendor re-attestations automatically.

header.heading: Accountability that stays current.

items.body: Every ROPA attestation is dated, owned, and still visible when the auditor asks who last confirmed it.

items.title: Vendor re-attestation on a clock
items.body: Stale processing terms surface before the assessment, not during it.

items.title: Evidence without the scramble

seo.title: Show the Board
seo.description: Board-ready privacy reporting drawn from the live estate: the trend, the target and the gap on one screen, with every number traceable to a record.

header.heading: Can you show the board where privacy stands, on one screen?
header.body: Boards do not want a walkthrough of a spreadsheet. They want the trend, the target and the gap. Pull those from the live estate rather than assembling them by hand each quarter, so the story is current and every number can be traced.

header.heading: The whole operation on one screen.
header.body: This is the Privacy Operations Centre. The row across the top is the state of play: tasks open, how many are past their target date, how many are still waiting on an owner, the average days to close and the share closed within SLA this year. Underneath, created against resolved over twelve months answers the question a board actually asks, whether the team is keeping up or falling behind, and the category breakdown shows where the work lands, from vendor assessments to subject rights requests. Every tile exports, and every number traces back to the tasks behind it.

media.alt: The Privacy Operations Centre dashboard, showing open, overdue and unassigned task counts above charts for status, monthly created against resolved volume, tasks by category and priority.

header.heading: Numbers with a trail.

items.title: Live posture, not a quarterly build
items.body: ROPA confirmation, vendor currency, open risks and overdue tasks are read from the estate, so the report is as current as the records behind it.

items.title: Target and gap on every measure
items.body: Set the target the board agreed and show the distance to it, with the trend since last quarter alongside.

items.title: Drill from the number to the record
items.body: Every figure links back to the activities, vendors or tasks behind it, so a challenge in the room has an answer.

header.heading: Show your board the trend, the target and the gap.
header.body: Book a demo to see the board view built from live records, and how every number drills to the activity, vendor or task behind it.

seo.title: Breach Response Readiness
seo.description: Breach response with roles, a running 72-hour clock and an evidence log built as decisions are made, tied to the systems and activities involved.

header.heading: It is 5pm on a Friday and someone has lost a laptop. Now what?
header.body: Seventy-two hours is not long when the first six are spent working out who is in charge and which systems were involved. Predefine the roles, start the clock at detection and log every decision as it is made, so the notification is evidenced rather than reconstructed.

data.quote: “The regulator will ask what you knew, when you knew it, and what you did in between.”

header.heading: The shape of your incidents, before the next one.
header.body: This is the breach readiness view. The top row is the current position: incidents open, how many are still awaiting triage, how many have been confirmed and how many have crossed the threshold for notifying a regulator. Below it, the pipeline shows where cases are stacked up and how long each stage is taking in practice, from triage through investigation and containment to closure. Severity and root cause sit alongside, so the pattern behind the incidents is something you can point at rather than something you suspect.

media.alt: The Breach Readiness dashboard, showing incident counts and notifications required above charts for incidents over time, stage pipeline and duration, severity distribution and root causes.

header.heading: Rehearsed, not improvised.

items.title: Roles set before the incident
items.body: Triage lead, DPO, comms and legal are named in advance, each with a fallback, so nobody is deciding who decides at 5pm on a Friday.

items.title: The clock starts at detection
items.body: Every action is timestamped against the 72-hour deadline, so you always know how much runway is left and can show how you used it.

items.title: Blast radius from the map
items.body: Link the incident to the systems involved and the estate shows the processing activities, vendors and data subjects affected.

header.heading: Rehearse the Friday breach before it happens.
header.body: Book a demo to see the roles, the 72-hour clock and the evidence log working together on a live incident walkthrough.

seo.title: Conflicting Sources of Truth
seo.description: Stop reconciling spreadsheets, registers and trackers that disagree. One connected privacy estate gives every processing activity a single, current record.

header.heading: Five tools, five answers. Which one does the regulator get?
header.body: When the ROPA lives in one spreadsheet, the vendor list in another and the DPIA register on a shared drive, every question about a processing activity has several answers. Connect them into one estate so a record has one owner, one status and one story.

data.quote: “A privacy programme is never more accurate than the least-maintained spreadsheet it depends on.”

header.heading: Every register reporting into one screen.
header.body: This is the screen the morning starts on. Programme at a glance holds each register as a tile, operational assessments, third parties, the ROPA, risks, incidents, subject rights and tasks, giving the counts a stack of spreadsheets would give you, except they are drawn from one estate rather than eight and they agree with each other. The line under the greeting is the one that matters on a Monday: how many items are overdue, and how many of those carry a statutory deadline. Scope it to your own work, your team's, or everything you can see.

media.alt: The platform dashboard, showing overdue and upcoming item counts above a programme at a glance panel with tiles for assessments, third parties, ROPA, risk, incidents, subject rights, tasks and the operations centre.

header.heading: One record, every angle.

items.title: One processing record
items.body: Each activity holds its systems, vendors, lawful basis and retention in one place. The ROPA, vendor register and DPIA log become views of the same data, not rivals to it.

items.title: Change once, reflect everywhere
items.body: Update a retention period on the record and every export, register and dashboard picks it up. There is no second copy to forget.

items.title: Provenance you can show
items.body: Every field carries who set it and when, so a challenged value has an answer rather than a shrug.

header.heading: One record, one answer. Bring a real example.
header.body: Book a 25-minute demo and bring a processing activity that lives in more than one place. We will show you what it looks like as a single connected record.

seo.title: Assessments That Land
seo.description: Connect every DPIA to the live risk it identified. Mitigations get owners and deadlines, and the assessment stays attached to the processing it covers.

header.heading: Your DPIA found the risk. Did anything happen next?
header.body: Too many assessments end as a signed PDF in a folder. Tie each DPIA to the processing activity it assessed and the risks it raised, so mitigations have owners, deadlines and a live status that someone is accountable for.

header.heading: Every assessment, and where it has got to.
header.body: This is the DPIA Review board. Every assessment sits in a column for not started, in progress, under review or complete, with the total, active and archived counts across the top. Each card carries who raised it, when it was last touched and whether the processing it covers is still live, so you can see which risks have someone working on them and which have stalled since sign-off. Search, filter or export the lot to Excel when the auditor asks.

media.alt: The DPIA Review board showing assessments as cards in columns for not started, in progress, under review and complete, with total, active and archived counts above.

header.heading: From finding to fix.

items.title: Risks become tasks
items.body: Each identified risk turns into a mitigation with an owner and a date, routed to the person who can actually close it.

items.title: Attached to the record
items.body: The DPIA sits on the processing activity it assessed. Open the record and the assessment, its risks and their status are right there.

items.title: Re-assessment triggers
items.body: When the activity changes materially, the platform flags the DPIA for review rather than leaving it to memory.

header.heading: Turn your last DPIA into tasks with owners.
header.body: Book a demo and bring an assessment you have already signed off. We will show how its risks become tracked mitigations attached to the live record.

header.heading: More than five DSARs a month, and you can't keep up?
header.body: Stop manually chasing department leads for data locations. When your estate is connected to operational systems, locating data subject records takes minutes instead of weeks.

data.quote: “Regulators don't measure good intentions; they measure statutory deadlines.”

header.heading: Every open request against its statutory clock.
header.body: This is the DSAR Overview. Across the top sit the numbers that matter on a Monday morning: how many requests are open, how many arrived this month, how many are past their statutory deadline or due within seven days, which have extensions running and the share closed inside 30 days. Below that the requests break down by the right being exercised, the channel they came in through, the volume month by month and where identity verification has got to, so you can see the pattern behind the backlog rather than one request at a time.

media.alt: The DSAR Overview dashboard with counts of open, new, overdue and due-soon requests, the SLA met rate, and charts breaking requests down by right type, monthly volume, intake channel and identity verification status.

items.title: Routed collection tasks

items.title: Incident linkage

header.heading: See a DSAR resolved against the map.

seo.title: Shadow AI
seo.description: Find every AI tool in use across the business, tie it to a processing record and govern it before it ships, not after.

header.heading: How many AI tools is your business using that privacy has never seen?
header.body: Teams adopt assistants, transcription tools and copilots faster than any intake form can catch them. Surface every AI tool in use, record what data it touches and attach it to a processing activity, so it is governed before it ships rather than discovered after.

header.heading: Eight of your forty-two activities are running AI.
header.body: This is the ROPA view filtered by AI capability. Eight processing activities come back, each drawn with the vendors, assets, risks and legal bases already attached to it, so an assistant somebody signed up for in Marketing arrives with its hallucination and data leakage risks on the record rather than in a conversation months later. The panel on the right stacks the conditions: generative AI as the capability, the named vendors behind it, the department functions that own them. The counts on the left tell you what the filter left standing.

media.alt: The ROPA view filtered by AI capability, showing eight processing activities as linked node clusters with a filter panel for vendors, assets, risks and legal bases.

header.heading: Governed before it ships.

items.title: An AI tool register
items.body: A dedicated register of AI tools, models and their vendors, each tied to the activity it serves and the personal data it processes.

items.title: Intake that fits how teams work
items.body: A short, plain-English intake that owners will actually complete, routed to privacy for review before the tool goes live.

items.title: Risk flags that follow the tool
items.body: Training on personal data, third-country transfers and automated decisions are flagged on the record, ready for the DPIA.

header.heading: Find the AI tools nobody told privacy about.
header.body: Book a demo to see the AI register, the intake teams will actually complete, and the risk flags that carry through to the DPIA.

seo.title: The Stale ROPA
seo.description: Keep the record of processing current between audits. Owners in the business re-confirm their activities as they change, so the ROPA never needs rebuilding.

header.heading: When did the business last confirm your Article 30 record was true?
header.body: A ROPA rebuilt in the fortnight before an audit is a snapshot of a rush, not a record of processing. Put confirmation in the hands of the people who own each activity, on a schedule, so the register stays current between audits rather than being reconstructed for them.

header.heading: See at a glance which records are still true.
header.body: This is the Visual ROPA View in review status mode. Every processing activity is a node, coloured by where its owner's confirmation stands: green when it is complete, purple while it is under review, red when it has not started. Filter by vendor, asset, risk or legal basis, and the register shows you where to chase next instead of leaving you to hunt through a spreadsheet.

media.alt: The Visual ROPA View in review status mode, showing every processing activity as a node with complete, in progress and not started records picked out by colour.

header.heading: A register that keeps itself honest.

items.title: Owner attestation on a cadence
items.body: Each activity has a named owner who confirms it on a schedule you set. Quarterly for high-risk processing, annually for the rest.

items.title: Change-triggered review
items.body: A new system, vendor or purpose flags the record for re-confirmation instead of waiting for the next cycle to come round.

items.title: Freshness at a glance
items.body: See which records are current, due and overdue across the estate, and chase by exception rather than by spreadsheet.

header.heading: See a ROPA that confirms itself.
header.body: Book a demo to see owner attestation in action: the schedule, the reminders and the freshness view that shows what is current, due and overdue.

seo.title: Culture & Training Alignment
seo.description: Align educational initiatives with actual operational risk markers derived from data activities and incident logs.

header.heading: Stop guessing where your risk actually sits.
header.body: Generic annual privacy training tick-boxes don't prevent data breaches. Align your educational initiatives with actual operational risk markers derived from data activities and incident logs.

header.heading: The teams that need more than a module.
header.body: This is the culture hot spots grid. Every business function sits against every location, and each cell carries two numbers: the culture score in bold and the participation rate beneath it. Colour runs from green where the score holds up to red where it does not, so a team that looks fine on the company average stops looking fine here. Overlay any two metrics, including incidents and training hours, and the confidence slider drops cells with too few responses to trust. Empty rows and columns hide themselves, so you are reading signal rather than grid.

media.alt: A colour-coded grid of culture scores and participation rates by business function and location, with metric tabs, a two-metric overlay and a confidence slider.

header.heading: Train the gap, not the average.

items.title: CultureLens sentiment
items.body: See where people believe they are strong, and where confidence is running ahead of the evidence.

items.title: Operational risk markers
items.body: Incident logs, stale processing, and high-risk activities mark the teams that need more than an annual course.

items.title: Education that follows the gap
items.body: Point budget at the cells where high confidence meets high operational risk, not at another generic module.

header.heading: Point the training budget where the risk actually is.
header.body: Book a demo to see CultureLens sentiment set against operational risk markers, and where the blind spots sit in your business.

seo.title: Vendor Risk That Goes Quiet
seo.description: Vendors watched continuously, not vetted once. Re-attestation schedules, sub-processor tracking and a live link from every processor to the activities it supports.

header.heading: You vetted the vendor two years ago. Who has checked since?
header.body: Due diligence at onboarding is a moment. Vendors change sub-processors, move data, get acquired and let certifications lapse. Keep processors on a re-attestation schedule and tie them to the activities they serve, so a change on their side becomes a task on yours.

header.heading: The vendors that need you this week.
header.body: This is the third parties requiring attention list. Every processor on it has a reason to be there: a high risk rating, a DPA that is still pending or was never signed, or an assessment that has never happened. Each row shows the business unit that owns the relationship, the current DPA status, when the vendor was last assessed and when the next review falls due, with overdue dates picked out in red. Export it to CSV when procurement or the auditor wants the list.

media.alt: A table of third parties requiring attention, listing each vendor's category, business unit, risk rating, DPA status, last assessment, next review date and the reason it needs attention.

header.heading: Onboarding is where it starts, not where it ends.

items.title: Re-attestation on a clock
items.body: Every processor carries a review date. Terms, certifications and sub-processor lists are re-confirmed before they go stale, not after.

items.title: Sub-processor changes tracked
items.body: Log each sub-processor a vendor uses and keep the change history, so a quiet move of data to a new region is visible when it happens.

items.title: Impact you can trace
items.body: A vendor issue shows every processing activity, system and data subject group it touches, so the response is proportionate rather than guessed.

header.heading: Put your processors on a clock.
header.body: Book a demo to see re-attestation schedules, sub-processor change tracking and the trace from a vendor issue to every activity it touches.
